findings.reason: the plan's deliverable, its second fixture and its second negative control all rest on a review-pass defect the callee's default already closes, so a node builds and gates a half that is not there.
findings.text: §9 says "The same sweep also launches the review reflex, so an observing follower can review a peer's run as well as resume it", but on main the review pass self-scopes: `dispatch_awaiting_reviews` resolves an unset `session` through `_sweeping_session` (`reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:1000`), which returns the session whose registration names `os.getpid()` (`reckon/crew/follower_registration.py:356`), i.e. the observing follower's *owning* session — so a peer's scoring run is skipped at `recovery_review_acceptance.py:404`. `tests/test_review_lane_follows_its_run.py::test_the_sweep_bookends_only_its_own_sessions_runs lands a claim that `dispatch_awaiting_reviews` called with no `session=` composes only `r-mine` and never `r-theirs` (session "session-someone-else") — held since 5b98a1c2f, 2026-09-23. The plan's "Confirmed on main on 2026-10-16" was taken only for the resume call site; the cited measurement (path-map question 3, 2026-09-22) predates the review pass's own fix. Only the resume pass (`list_live(project=project)`, `resumption.py:1688`, no session filter) is still a live leak from an observing follower.

findings.reason: an unfalsifiable control is exactly what the rubric forbids in a done-when, and this one masks whether the review half is a defect at all.
findings.text: the second declared negative control, "calling the review-reflex pass without the session, and the observed session's scoring run is then reviewed and the test fails", cannot fail: calling `dispatch_awaiting_reviews` without `session=` inside a follower already filters to the follower's session, so the observed run is not reviewed and the test stays green with the control in place. A control that holds however the code behaves measures nothing, and the node's gate could not show its guard firing.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_sweep_lapsed_holds` resolves in `reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:93`, `sweep` in `reckon/crew/resumption.py:1651`, `watch` in `reckon/crew/runs.py:3081`, the measurement plan §7 and the cited re-arm figures resolve, and the path map's staleness claim is confirmed (`docs/research/data/monitor-scope-path-map.json` still cites `reckon/cli.py:1793…2256`). Minor: `dispatch_awaiting_reviews` is *defined* in `reckon/crew/recovery_review_acceptance.py:360` and only imported/called in `resumption.py:1888`; the plan's parenthetical already names the defining file, so it resolves.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §9 declares two negative controls, but the second (the review-reflex control at :209) cannot go red, because the pass it disables already scopes itself to the sweeping follower's session.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the done-when names `tests/test_follow_sweep_is_session_scoped.py` under the repository, and the write paths are existing source modules; nothing lands in a session scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the new test name states its mechanism, and no plan label, stage name or ticket number reaches a symbol, filename or comment.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §9's stated root cause for the review-reflex half does not match the code it cites: the review pass is already session-scoped, so the leak the plan blames is not live on main.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §9 names one mechanism (scope the sweep to the session that owns the runs), with the watcher sweep as its second, locked half; each half carries its own discriminating case (the nine-minute boundary for the watcher, the lapsed hold for the follower).
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §9 is covered by the open followup `f-tmstwiw-open-sections` ("Build the open monitor sections (§7–§12)"), which carries a one-line invocation at the §7 boundary, and no dependency it needs is unstated.
